quoteAnchors.analysis: Preserves the existing real-lexer leading-token check (mori_lexer::first_token_text) without introducing any ad-hoc string prefix detection; sources that do not begin with a lexed 'language' token after whitespace and comments continue to route to the Beta parser/checker unchanged.

Replaces the previous `mori_core::language(source).is_ok_and(|language| language == "moriarty/2")` boolean collapse with an explicit match on `mori_core::language(source)` so that header routing errors are not discarded in favor of a Core1-only `mori_core::parse(source)` fallback.

Propagates the exact `mori_core::Error` from `mori_core::language(source)` directly into `consumer.core(Err(error), false)`, preserving dual-profile (`"moriarty/1"` or `"moriarty/2"`) error messages, codes (`mori::core::profile` or `mori::core::syntax`), UTF-8 byte offsets, full-lex error precedence (`mori::core::lex`), and `staged = false` so `/2` stage qualification labels are omitted when no profile was admitted.
Retains the exact existing Core1 (`mori_core::parse`) vs staged Core2 (`mori_core::stage::load`) selection when `mori_core::language(source)` succeeds with `"moriarty/1"` or `"moriarty/2"`.

Ensures `core_report` only attaches `mori_core::stage::STAGE_LABELS` (`qualification`, `authentication`, `consumption`) when `staged` is true, so failed header routing (`staged = false`) emits only `diagnostics`, `file`, and `status: "rejected"`.

Verifies the complete `--json` stdout byte stream against `expected_stdout.as_bytes()` after checking exit status 1; in RED, all three test functions panicked on this exact line because the unpatched binary emitted Core1-only messages.

Constructs the expected normal-verbosity stderr output by prepending the Cargo-style `    Checking header.mori\n` status line to the quiet stderr diagnostic, verifying that normal and quiet human modes preserve the existing `Shell` rendering path on stderr while leaving stdout empty.

Tests an unknown profile string (`language "other";`) across JSON, quiet human, and normal human CLI invocations, asserting code `mori::core::profile`, UTF-8 byte offset 16 (the `;` token after `"other"`), `step: null`, and the dual-profile message naming both `"moriarty/1"` and `"moriarty/2"`.

Tests a missing profile string literal (`language ;`), asserting code `mori::core::syntax`, UTF-8 byte offset 9 (the `;` token), `step: null`, and the prepended dual-profile expectation message (`Expected language "moriarty/1" or "moriarty/2". Expected a quoted string.`).

Tests a leading UTF-8 comment (`// café\nlanguage "other";` where `é` is 2 UTF-8 bytes) before the `language` header, confirming that `first_token_text` skips comments and `mori_core::language` reports the exact UTF-8 byte offset 25 (`9 + 16`).

sourceAssessment.reason: The two-path change in commit 5f7c2a28efb69d36e171d85ffd39bf59f8e68c68 is minimal, well-scoped, and faithful to the existing architecture and contracts. In crates/mori/src/commands/check_source.rs (a53d5c3689f3c32ddc8c595e577a0ac13cfc4fe187b42a4f83c9caf86dc9ace3), dispatch() previously called `mori_core::language(source).is_ok_and(|language| language == "moriarty/2")` after `mori_lexer::first_token_text(source)` identified a leading `"language"` token. Whenever `mori_core::language(source)` returned `Err(error)` (such as an unknown profile `"other"` or missing profile string `language ;`), `is_ok_and` collapsed that `Err` to `staged = false` and ran `mori_core::parse(source)` (the Core1 parser), which overwrote the routing reader's dual-profile diagnostic (`Expected language "moriarty/1" or "moriarty/2"...`, already frozen in `crates/mori-core/tests/language.rs`) with a Core1-only diagnostic (`Expected language "moriarty/1"; found "other".` or `Expected a quoted string.`). Matching on `mori_core::language(source)` and returning `consumer.core(Err(error), false)` on `Err` propagates the existing `mori_core::Error` unchanged through `CliConsumer::core`: `--json` serializes the rejected report via `core_report` and `mori_core::json::export` without `/2` `STAGE_LABELS` (`staged = false`), while human normal and quiet modes render `error: {code}: {message}` on stderr via `Shell::error` (with `    Checking <file>` on stderr only in non-quiet, non-JSON mode) and exit with code 1. Because `mori_core::language(source)` calls `mori_lexer::lex(source)` before inspecting header tokens, full-source lexical errors still take precedence and produce the identical `mori::core::lex` `Error`. All accepted and rejected `moriarty/1` and `moriarty/2` paths after header selection, as well as the entire Beta branch and non-`"language"` leading-token dispatch, are untouched. The companion integration test crates/mori/tests/check_header_dispatch.rs (436ed1f95be58430ad9b0aa6ce2af38b8d1c6f9fd8fa37ebc5d2dedc7e316bb4) follows the established `check_source_dispatch.rs` real-binary pattern and tests unknown profile, missing profile string, and UTF-8 commented header cases across `--json`, `--quiet`, and normal human modes, checking exit code 1, UTF-8 byte offsets (16, 9, 25), `step: null`, and exact stdout/stderr bytes. Both files pass Rust 1.99.0 rustfmt (`--edition 2024 --check`) and respect UNI-018 and the Rust diagnostics/testing/CLI guidelines.
